public_source.record: Friedman 1997 construction; current best-known upper bound, checked 2026-11-05

limitations: This is a feasible upper bound. The optimum remains open.

verification.source_review: Sol checked the current squaremath.org exact-parameter record, replayed the saved certificate, independently computed the enclosing side, rejected a damaged construction, and confirmed that a forged objective cannot change the result.

best_human.provenance: Erich Friedman, 1997, Section 3, Figure 9. The published construction family formula gives side (7+3√2)/2. The saved witness was reconstructed from that formula and the stated off-center construction.
best_human.evidence_state: published construction reconstructed from its explicit formula and independently certified exactly

best_public.origin_type: unknown unless attribution is stated in source/provenance

best_reproduced.provenance: Reconstructed from Friedman's 1997 Section 3 formula for (a,b)=(2,3): a 3×3 block of 45-degree squares, axis-aligned frame squares selected by exact separation checks, and the added column of five squares.
best_reproduced.ai_provenance: Reconstructed for this benchmark from the published formula; not represented as a verbatim transcription of the diagram.
best_reproduced.evidence_state: all 26 squares, exact Q(sqrt(2)) corners, all 325 pair checks, and bounding square independently certified

survey_scope_note: Best public means the strongest same-parameter result in the cited checked sources. This is not a claim that every public source has been surveyed. Unmatched parameters are listed separately.
